group.passage: Have you ever drawn a little stick figure in the corner of every page of a notebook and then flipped the pages fast? If you have, you have made a flip book, and you have used the same idea that is behind every cartoon. In 1868, an English printer named John Barnes Linnett got a patent for a small book of pictures like this. He called it a kineograph, a name that means “moving picture.” A flip book works through a trick of the eye: when the pictures pass by quickly, our eyes cannot see them one at a time, so they blend into smooth movement. Each page is like one frame of a film, and each picture is only a little different from the one before it. In this way, the flip book pointed the way to motion pictures. Soon artists began to put their drawings on film. In 1906, J. Stuart Blackton filmed himself drawing funny faces and then made the faces move. A little later, the French artist Emile Cohl made a short film from about 700 drawings. It lasted less than two minutes. The most famous early cartoon star was a dinosaur. In 1914, Winsor McCay showed Gertie the Dinosaur at a theater in Chicago. He stood on the stage with a whip and gave Gertie orders, and at one point he seemed to feed her an apple. Many people in the audience believed she was real. Making so many drawings took a long time, so McCay found a way to save work. To show Gertie breathing, he filmed the same set of drawings again and again, up to fifteen times. Cartoons kept growing. In 1937, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs became the first full-length cartoon film made in the United States, and more than 750 artists worked on it. Yet it still used the simple idea of the flip book: many pictures, each a little different, shown one after another.

translation_zh.text:
你有沒有在筆記本每一頁的角落畫一個小火柴人，然後快速翻動書頁？如果有，你就做出了一本翻頁書，而且你用到的正是每一部卡通背後的同一個原理。1868 年，一位名叫約翰．巴恩斯．林奈特的英國印刷商替這樣一本小圖畫書取得了專利。他把它叫做 kineograph，這個名字的意思是「會動的圖畫」。
翻頁書靠的是一種眼睛的錯覺：當圖畫很快地閃過時，我們的眼睛無法一張一張分開來看，於是它們就融合成流暢的動作。每一頁就像影片的一格畫面，而每一張圖都只和前一張有一點點不同。就這樣，翻頁書為電影指出了方向。
不久之後，藝術家開始把自己的畫放到影片上。1906 年，J．史都華．布萊克頓拍下自己畫滑稽臉孔的過程，然後讓那些臉孔動起來。稍後，法國藝術家埃米爾．科爾用大約 700 張圖畫做出一部短片，片長不到兩分鐘。
早期最有名的卡通明星是一隻恐龍。1914 年，溫莎．麥凱在芝加哥的一家戲院放映《恐龍葛蒂》。他拿著鞭子站在舞台上對葛蒂下指令，有一幕他甚至好像在餵她吃蘋果。台下許多觀眾都相信她是真的。畫這麼多圖要花很長的時間，所以麥凱想出了一個省工的方法。為了表現葛蒂在呼吸，他把同一組圖畫反覆拍攝，最多拍了十五次。
卡通不斷發展。1937 年，《白雪公主與七矮人》成為美國第一部長篇卡通電影，有超過 750 位畫家參與製作。不過，它用的仍然是翻頁書那個簡單的原理：許多張圖畫，每張只有一點點不同，一張接一張地播放。
